relationships.evidence_quote: zinc has a high-affinity binding site on the lysine-133 residue in the extracellular domain of ASIC1a channels, where it exhibits inhibitory behavior

relationships.subject: zinc
relationships.evidence_quote: Zinc binds to the extracellular domain of ASIC1b channels and displays inhibitory mechanisms

relationships.subject: zinc
relationships.evidence_quote: unlike ASIC1b, zinc inhibits both the peak and sustained component in ASIC3

relationships.subject: zinc
relationships.evidence_quote: Co-application of zinc dose-dependently potentiated the peak and sustained component of ASIC1a/3 channels.

relationships.subject: zinc
relationships.evidence_quote: Zinc serves as a negative modulator for all calcium channels

key_findings: Zinc modulates ASICs in a subtype-dependent manner: inhibiting ASIC1a, ASIC1b and ASIC3, potentiating ASIC1a/3 and ASIC2a-containing channels.
Zinc-binding sites include K133 in ASIC1a and C196 in human ASIC1b.
